quizzes.stem: A team moves a working direct-API request to Google Cloud, swaps the API key for a Google access token and keeps the body unchanged. It is refused. Which changes does the page require?

options.a: Prefix the model with the provider name and keep the version as a header
options.b: Keep the model in the payload and move the version into the payload too
options.c: Move both the model and the version into the query string of the address
options.d: Name the model in the address and carry the version in the payload

explanation.d: The page says "`model` is not passed in the request body" and that it "is specified in the Google Cloud endpoint URL", while `anthropic_version` goes "in the request body".
explanation.b: Ruled out because moving the version is right but the model must leave the body: "Vertex wants the model in the URL".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the model sits in the address path, "before `:rawPredict`", and "The version is the body field" `anthropic_version`, not a query parameter.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The model id there is the plain name", with no prefix, and the version is passed "rather than as a header".

quizzes.stem: A developer calls Claude Opus 5.5 through Bedrock with the identifier `claude-opus-5-5` and gets an error. What fixes it?

options.a: Keep the id in the body and put the anthropic. prefix in front of it
options.b: Use the dated id that the direct API lists for this same model
options.c: Use the Google Cloud form of the id, with an at sign and a date
options.d: Move the id into the endpoint address and leave it out of the body

explanation.a: The page says "Model IDs in Claude in Amazon Bedrock carry an `anthropic.` provider prefix", and the model stays in the body.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the id gains a prefix, not a date: "so `claude-opus-5-5` becomes `anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the at-sign form is the Google Cloud one, "with a dated form for some models", and there the model sits in the URL.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the model stays in the body on Bedrock, "the same request body shape as Anthropic's first-party API".

quizzes.stem: A security team wants no long-lived keys on developer laptops when calling Claude through Bedrock. Which path does the page favour?

options.a: An Anthropic API key per developer, rotated by the security team monthly
options.b: Bearer tokens kept in each laptop's configuration file for daily use
options.c: A provisioned service role that the platform assumes for the caller
options.d: An assumed role with a session that lasts for a full working week

explanation.c: The page marks the service role as the recommended path: "Use a Bedrock service role with AWS-managed keys for the most secure, long-lived access".
explanation.b: Ruled out because bearer tokens are "(12-hour maximum, least preferred)".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Neither platform needs an Anthropic API key", however often it is rotated.
explanation.d: Ruled out because an assumed role has "a 12-hour maximum session", not a week.

quizzes.stem: A team on Amazon Bedrock plans nightly bulk jobs through the Message Batches API at half price. What should it budget?

options.a: Batch jobs on Bedrock, at the same half price as on the direct API
options.b: Ordinary one-by-one calls, at the usual per-token rate with no discount
options.c: Batch jobs on Bedrock, at half price plus a ten percent regional premium
options.d: Batch jobs on Bedrock, with the inputs uploaded through the Files API

explanation.b: The Bedrock page lists "API endpoints (Message Batches, Models, Admin, Compliance, Usage and Cost)" under features not supported, and the discount "belongs to the Message Batches API".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Bedrock has no such endpoint on this integration".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the premium belongs to regional routing, "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints.", and there is no batch endpoint to apply it to.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the Files API is itself on the list: "URL sources for images and documents, Files API".

quizzes.stem: A company must keep its Claude traffic on Google Cloud inside one named region and also wants provisioned throughput. Which type of address fits?

options.a: A regional kind for residency, with the global kind for throughput
options.b: The global kind, since it routes to wherever capacity is free today
options.c: The multi-region kind, since it supports provisioned throughput as well
options.d: The regional kind, since it serves both of the needs at a 10% premium

explanation.d: The page says regional endpoints are "Required for single-region data residency, strict compliance mandates, or provisioned throughput", at the premium.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the global kind will "Dynamically route requests to regions with available capacity", so traffic leaves the one region.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the multi-region kind also "supports pay-as-you-go traffic only".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the global kind "only supports pay-as-you-go traffic (provisioned throughput requires regional endpoints)", so the reserved capacity cannot sit there.

quizzes.stem: A team must pick between the two partner platforms and needs structured outputs and web search from it. What do the pages show?

options.a: Bedrock offers web search only, while Google Cloud offers both of them
options.b: Bedrock offers neither one, while Google Cloud offers both of them
options.c: Both offer the two features, since each takes the same request body
options.d: Google Cloud offers structured outputs only, while Bedrock offers both

explanation.b: The page says "Web search and structured outputs are on Google Cloud and not on Bedrock."
explanation.a: Ruled out because Bedrock's list has "Server-side tools (code execution, web search, web fetch, advisor)" as missing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a shared body does not mean shared features: Google Cloud "does offer more than Bedrock in two places".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the Google Cloud page lists both "among its supported feature highlights", and Bedrock lists structured outputs under its gaps.

quizzes.stem: A team moves its Bedrock traffic from the global endpoint to a regional one for data residency. The same tokens cost 1,000 dollars a month before. What should it budget now?

options.a: About 1,000, since the same models serve both of the routes
options.b: About 1,100, since that route is priced above the dynamic one
options.c: About 900, since the global route was the one with the premium
options.d: About 500, since that route runs on spare capacity at half price

explanation.b: The page says "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints.", so 1,000 becomes about 1,100.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Bedrock has the same idea with different words" as Google Cloud, where regional endpoints "include a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a global endpoint gives "dynamic routing across all available regions for maximum availability" with no premium.
explanation.d: Ruled out because half price is a different route: "the 50 percent discount of module 21 belongs to the Message Batches API".

quizzes.stem: build_request is called for Vertex with claude-opus-5-5 and a single named region. What happens?

options.a: It raises PlatformError for the endpoint field, as newer models use other routes
options.b: It builds the URL with the region host, as every model is served by those hosts
options.c: It falls back to the worldwide host without complaint and returns the request
options.d: It raises PlatformError for the model field, as that model id is not known

explanation.a: The page's comment is "Specific regional endpoints support Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier; newer models use the global or multi-region endpoints", and the practice says a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the specific regional endpoints serve only older models".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the practice states "An unsupported model and endpoint pair is a `PlatformError`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only", so the model is known and the endpoint is the fault.

quizzes.stem: A team wants the faster output mode for its streamed chat on Opus 5.5 and may call Claude from any platform. Where can it get it?

options.a: The direct API, since the option is offered on that door alone
options.b: Google Cloud, since it offers more features than Bedrock does
options.c: Claude Platform on AWS, since Anthropic itself operates that door
options.d: Bedrock or Google Cloud, once a beta header is sent with the call

explanation.a: The page says fast mode "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "One more gap spans the partner platforms", and Google Cloud is one of them.
explanation.c: Ruled out because fast mode "is not available on Claude Platform on AWS", although Anthropic operates it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a header does not change that: "not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms".

quizzes.stem: A team's Bedrock traffic needs 4 million input tokens per minute. What do the docs say?

options.a: It sits beyond every limit, so a second account is needed
options.b: It fits inside the default, so nothing extra is asked of anyone
options.c: It exceeds the default but stays beneath the requestable ceiling
options.d: It follows the direct API quota rather than the cloud one

explanation.c: The page gives "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM without additional Anthropic approval."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and 4 million exceeds it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "You can request up to 5 million input TPM" covers 4 million.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "AWS enforces requests-per-minute (RPM) limits on the Bedrock side".
